paras: The threatened lynching of William Utley and Henry Fisher took place at Springfield, Tennessee, in late June 1881, after the two Black men were jailed on the night of June 27 on a charge of attempting to assault a white woman, Mrs. Mattie Davis. A Nashville dispatch predicted they would be lynched before morning, and a later brief said the people of Springfield had made preparations to lynch them. No report of the outcome was found.

According to the dispatch dated Nashville, June 27, Utley and Fisher, described as 'negroes', were lodged in the Springfield jail that night for an 'attempted outrage' on Mattie Davis, identified as white. Other copies called the charge an 'attempted assault' or an 'attempted rape', and a version dated June 28 placed the jailing on 'Monday night'. The dispatch closed with the expectation that the men would 'probably be lynched before morning'.

Two days later a news digest reported that 'the people of Springfield, Tenn., have made preparations to lynch two negroes in jail for an outrage on a white lady', without naming the men. No account of an attack on the jail, a removal of the prisoners, or a killing appears in the coverage.
The coverage does not show whether Utley and Fisher were lynched, tried or released, and no later report on the case was found.

The story reached papers only as a short telegram, which ran on June 28 in the Wheeling Register under the head 'Prospective Hemp Stretching' and in the New-York Tribune under 'Lynching Threatened in Tennessee'. The Dallas Daily Herald, the Weekly Clarion of Jackson, Mississippi, and The People and New Hampshire Patriot carried versions over the next two days, with the names variously printed as Uttey, Tuley, Frizer, Fizer, Fizier and Trice. Each stated the accusation as the charge and treated the coming lynching as expected, without comment.
The 'preparations to lynch' line ran as a one-sentence item in the Wheeling Register's digest on June 30 and again in the Mineral Point Tribune's 'Criminal' column on July 7.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of William Utley and Henry Fisher
bases: Two Black men jailed on an assault charge were reported likely to be lynched, and a later brief said townspeople had prepared to lynch them, but no killing is reported (A1, A2, A5).

The papers report only a predicted lynching and 'preparations to lynch' by the people of Springfield; no report says the men were killed, released or tried (A1, A2, A5). The threat was extralegal and tied to an accusation of attempted assault on a white woman, but no killing is documented.
Every report descends from one Nashville dispatch of June 27-28 (A1, A2, A7) and one unattributed news-digest brief (A5); no local or independent account was found.
